sections.heading: Vectors & Embeddings in AI Practice Exercises

questions.q: Compute the dot product of the embedding vector \( \mathbf{u} = [2, 3]^T \) with itself.
questions.answer: The dot product with itself is the squared Euclidean norm: \( \mathbf{u} \cdot \mathbf{u} = (2)^2 + (3)^2 = 4 + 9 = 13 \).

questions.q: Compute the dot product of the embedding vector \( \mathbf{u} = [3, 4]^T \) with itself.
questions.answer: The dot product with itself is the squared Euclidean norm: \( \mathbf{u} \cdot \mathbf{u} = (3)^2 + (4)^2 = 9 + 16 = 25 \).

questions.q: Compute the dot product of the embedding vector \( \mathbf{u} = [4, 5]^T \) with itself.
questions.answer: The dot product with itself is the squared Euclidean norm: \( \mathbf{u} \cdot \mathbf{u} = (4)^2 + (5)^2 = 16 + 25 = 41 \).

questions.q: Compute the dot product of the embedding vector \( \mathbf{u} = [5, 6]^T \) with itself.
questions.answer: The dot product with itself is the squared Euclidean norm: \( \mathbf{u} \cdot \mathbf{u} = (5)^2 + (6)^2 = 25 + 36 = 61 \).

questions.q: Compute the dot product of the embedding vector \( \mathbf{u} = [6, 7]^T \) with itself.
questions.answer: The dot product with itself is the squared Euclidean norm: \( \mathbf{u} \cdot \mathbf{u} = (6)^2 + (7)^2 = 36 + 49 = 85 \).

questions.q: Compute the dot product of the embedding vector \( \mathbf{u} = [7, 8]^T \) with itself.
questions.answer: The dot product with itself is the squared Euclidean norm: \( \mathbf{u} \cdot \mathbf{u} = (7)^2 + (8)^2 = 49 + 64 = 113 \).

questions.q: Compute the Manhattan (\( L_1 \)) norm and Euclidean (\( L_2 \)) norm of the word vector \( \mathbf{w} = [2, -3]^T \).
questions.answer: \( L_1 \) norm is the sum of absolute values: \( |2| + |-3| = 5 \). \( L_2 \) norm is the square root of sum of squares: \( \sqrt{(2)^2 + (-3)^2} = \sqrt{4 + 9} = \sqrt{13} \).

questions.q: Compute the Manhattan (\( L_1 \)) norm and Euclidean (\( L_2 \)) norm of the word vector \( \mathbf{w} = [4, -6]^T \).
questions.answer: \( L_1 \) norm is the sum of absolute values: \( |4| + |-6| = 10 \). \( L_2 \) norm is the square root of sum of squares: \( \sqrt{(4)^2 + (-6)^2} = \sqrt{16 + 36} = \sqrt{52} \).
